scenes.promptInstructions: SCENE 1 — BREAKING CLEAR, START FRAME BEFORE ANIMATION. TEMPLATE: Central player faces the camera nearly head-on, running hard with ONE red Australian rules football in BOTH hands low across his torso. An opposition defender on the LEFT is very close behind, reaching toward/touching the player's upper arm. Keep the defender's exact face, reaching arm and close separation as photographed: the escape happens later in the VIDEO, not in this image. Keep the runner's running-leg pose and close front-facing framing. There are NO visible goalposts. Replace ONLY the central player's full head (selfie face and hair) and selected-team playing kit as required by shared instructions. This MUST remain the exact same Scene 1 master photograph and frozen action pose, not a new runner or a newly generated action frame. The defender wears an unbranded black guernsey with a bold red diagonal sash, no badge, sponsor mark, lettering or logos. Do not move the ball, replace the defender, create another player, show a completed tackle, show a kick or insert goals. Focused, recognisable customer face, no forced grin.

SCENE 2 — REAR THREE-QUARTER PRE-KICK, EXACT APPROVED MASTER. The navy-clad athlete is LARGE in the FAR LEFT foreground, viewed from behind and slightly to the right, running FORWARD away from the camera and toward the goals. His head faces forward toward the goals, NOT back at the camera. ONE red AFL football is held low securely in BOTH HANDS and has not been dropped or kicked yet. Preserve his running pose, hands, ball, head angle and left framing. Match the customer's HAIR from the selfie and harmonise exposed skin; never turn the head or invent a frontal face. Dress only the central athlete in the selected team guernsey, shorts and socks, preserving the folds. Keep precisely FOUR EXISTING white goalposts ahead, on ONE goal line, with EVEN spacing, two taller central goalposts and outer behind posts at about FOUR-FIFTHS (80%) of the central height, each with its original red base padding. Do not add, remove or move posts. Preserve EXISTING distant blurred opposition defenders in unbranded BLACK guernseys with RED diagonal sashes, including ONE running TOWARD the ball-carrier; others watch him. Keep the stadium, lighting, grass, crowd and background faces, but remove any identifiable sponsor, league or club logos, lettering, advertising boards and branded signage visible in the master. NO ball flight, kick, extra people or camera-angle changes.

SCENE 3 — SOLO PREMIERS CELEBRATION, EXACT APPROVED MASTER FRAME. Central foreground player alone, facing the camera, mouth open in a triumphant natural shout with ONE clenched fist raised in front of his body; his other arm is down. TWO small teammates are already cheering several metres behind him, one on each side, separated from him and not touching him. Preserve the master camera angle, player proportions, precise fist and hand positions, distant teammates, faces, night stadium, crowd, bright floodlights and gently drifting GOLD CONFETTI. Replace ONLY the foreground player's entire visible head with the customer's recognisable selfie face, real hairstyle, age and natural expression; preserve the original orientation, visible teeth/mouth anatomy and lighting without exaggerated stretching. Harmonise the central player's visible skin as defined in shared instructions. Change the foreground player and the TWO distant teammates into matching unbranded playing kits with the selected colours and pattern, without modifying the background players' faces or positions. REMOVE any existing AFL/league badges, sponsor logos and manufacturer branding on chest, shorts or stadium signs, including all legible stadium text; use plain fabric and an unbranded blank illuminated display. Do not introduce an embrace, foreground teammates, new text, second fist, ball, trophies, extra people, new confetti bursts or camera changes.

sharedPrompt:
TASK: Precise photorealistic IMAGE EDIT, not a new scene generation. Two input images in order: Image 1 = the scene TEMPLATE, which controls framing, camera, action pose, football, other people, oval, lighting and stadium; Image 2 = the CUSTOMER SELFIE, the ONLY source for the central player's identity. Produce one sharp 9:16 Australian rules football broadcast-quality still using the template as the composition.

MASTER FRAME LOCK: Preserve Image 1 exactly in framing, pose, players, object positions and lighting; edit only head, playing kit, central-player skin blending and removal of existing branded marks from kit and stadium surfaces. Never redraw scenery or pose.

SCENE-SPECIFIC CAMERA RULE: In SCENES 1 and 3 the player's visible face remains the main identity target. In SCENE 2 the approved rear three-quarter master shows the athlete from behind: do not turn his head or force a front-facing swap. For SCENE 2, match the customer's actual hairstyle (length, texture, colour, hairline) from Image 2, visible ear or profile details only, and consistent complexion on visible skin. Preserve the camera, ball, body, four posts and defenders from Image 1. This rear-view exception overrides front-facing instructions below; never rotate the head.\n\nIDENTITY IS THE HIGHEST PRIORITY: Replace the central template player's entire visible head, including face, ears, hairline and hairstyle, with the actual individual in the selfie. Reproduce recognisable eye spacing/shape, brows, nose, lips, cheeks, jaw, age, distinctive texture and real hair length, colour and style. Do not retain the template man's facial features, generic handsome-athlete face, beard or hair. Do not de-age, beautify, enlarge the jaw, smooth wrinkles, add a smile or change ethnicity. The person must immediately be recognisable as the selfie subject, not a lookalike.

SKIN TONE AND LIGHTING — CRITICAL, EQUAL PRIORITY TO FACE IDENTITY: The uploaded CUSTOMER SELFIE determines the central player's natural complexion, not the template athlete's skin. After transferring the customer's entire recognisable head, harmonise the central player's ENTIRE visible skin from face through ears, jaw, neck, shoulders, upper arms, forearms, hands, thighs, knees and calves into ONE coherent natural skin tone. Recolour the template body's strongly orange/tanned/saturated skin to the customer's natural complexion; do NOT leave an orange muscular body attached to a pale face. Do NOT artificially tan, darken or redden the customer's face to match the old template body. Apply the same realistic night-stadium floodlight illumination, shadows, highlights, white balance and sweat texture across face, neck and all exposed limbs. No visible face-swap edge, colour seam at jaw/collar, contrasting hands or different neck colour. Check that face and nearest shoulder/arm could plausibly belong to the same person under the same lighting.

INTEGRATION: This must look like one naturally photographed person, NOT a pale face pasted onto a deep-tan body. Preserve the customer's recognisable facial structure, real skin texture, hairstyle, hairline and age while making head and body skin tones visually consistent. Preserve the template's running/celebration body pose, proportions, guernsey, hand positions and stadium composition. Avoid an exaggerated bodybuilder transformation. Keep the head correctly sized and oriented for the template. Do not blend the template athlete's facial identity into the customer. NEVER recolour the other players' skin or faces.

TEAM EDIT: Replace the central athlete's plain navy template guernsey with the selected unbranded guernsey colours/pattern, and recolour shorts and socks into a coordinated, plausible kit. Preserve fabric shape, folds, arms and the football. In Scene 3 only, recolour the TWO small, distant background teammates' existing guernseys to the selected unbranded colours/pattern; keep their faces, positions and bodies unchanged. They remain several metres behind the solo foreground player, with no physical contact. Opposition players are NOT the customer and must not be face-swapped or recoloured as teammates.

DO NOT RECOMPOSE: Keep the exact camera viewpoint, relative subject size and position, posture, foreground/background depth of field, crowd, existing goalposts where shown, lighting, ball placement, hands, other player positions, stadium display and existing confetti where shown. No new people, posts, balls, text, logos or accessories. REMOVE any existing club crests, sponsor logos, brand text, manufacturer badges, league insignia, advertising lettering and branded stadium signage from the template and resulting playing kits; replace markings with natural plain fabric or neutral blank surfaces. Keep the same scene geometry, original players, goalposts and stadium layout. No official insignia or sponsor marks anywhere in frame. Do not insert the selfie background. The central player remains the sole personalised identity. Output a natural, high-detail 9:16 vertical sports photograph.
